messages:
slo-monitor-bot: SLO burn alert: 5xx rate > 2% for api-gateway over 5m. Investigate: https://grafana.redwood-infra/g/alerts/5xx-spike (datadog link in card)

maria: seeing it too. 5xx spike started ~1901234400. Most are gateway timeouts / upstream 504s. Customer tickets piling in. @support-ops can you paste an example? :thinking:

support-ops: Customer ticket #C-4821 — multiple requests returning 504s and timeouts since ~10:40PT. They report long-running generation calls failing mid-token. Provided one request id: req_0a7f3e

raj: pulling logs. datadog query:

```
service:api-gateway env:prod status:[500 TO 599] @http.path:/v1/generate | top("http.upstream_status") by 5m
```

Most upstream_status are 504 and 502, with a tail of 500. Volume correlates with increased request latency.

leo: opening traces — many of the 504s have no downstream trace in the model-serving cluster. Tracing shows proxy timed out before request reached model container in ~60% of samples. Looks like proxy_read_timeout + ALB idle timeout mismatch on some long-lived streams.

emily: checked ALB logs -> a bump in "TargetResponseTime" and a bunch of 502/504 from targets at ~10:38-10:50. No node OOMs, but a subset of pods reporting high CPU and syscall sleep in top. Possible GC/blocked threads.

maria: quick repro: curl to gateway with a long prompt (approx 5k tokens) and stream=false sometimes returns 504 after ~30s.

```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-lite","input":"<long prompt>", "stream": false}' https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate
```

support-ops: customer confirms they use stream=false and have a single-shot long prompt. They saw spike when traffic increased.

raj: correlation query: KV cache miss rate jumped from 8% -> 36% for model:gpt-lite between 10:35-10:45. If KV cache misses cause longer inference setup, proxies hit timeouts.

leo: rolling restart of the worst CPU pods in model-serving reduced errors in that AZ. I kicked a restart for model-pool-gpt-lite-3.

maria: mitigation checklist I ran:
- bumped nginx proxy_read_timeout from 30s -> 90s on gateway canary
- enabled fast-fallback route to gpt-small for requests where prompt length > 2k tokens (temporary)
- increased retry budget for 502/504 to 2 with exponential backoff in the gateway

raj: logs show 5xx rate dropped ~60% after the above, but still some residual 502s from a specific node set (ip: 10.12.5.*). Investigating kernel-level blocking.

emily: I captured strace snapshot on a suspect pod — a bunch of syscalls stuck in epoll_wait; seems to line up with heavy GC pauses in the model runtime. Need GC tuning / newer runtime kernel flags.

leo: tracing gap note — sampling ratio for traces was reduced in the midnight config change (we lowered to 0.2). That made it hard to connect some 504s to model spans. I'll raise sampling to 0.6 during peak window for better coverage.

support-ops: customer C-4821 updated: degraded but usable after retrying 2x. They want root cause timeline and mitigation steps.

maria: next steps (action items):
- raj to add a Datadog monitor for KV cache miss rate > 20% (sensitive) (due: today)
- leo to add pod-level alert for syscall-blocked ratio > 5% on model pool (due: today)
- emily to open RFC for runtime GC tuning and schedule canary (due: this week)
- ops to document fallback routing pattern for long prompts (done inline)

raj: pushed a saved query to our docs: https://playbooks.redwood/internal/queries/kv-cache-miss

leo: will follow up with a postmortem if we see reoccurrence. For now error rate back to baseline ~1901235520.

slo-monitor-bot: Alert status: acknowledged by eng-sre. 5xx rate returned to baseline. Alert closed at 1901235623.

maria: summary for support: temporary mitigation = timeout bump + fallback to gpt-small + retries. Root cause likely a mix of KV cache miss spike + model runtime GC/blocked threads -> upstream slow responses -> gateway timeouts. Follow-ups scheduled.

support-ops: I'll update the customer ticket with the summary and ETA for follow-ups. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
